focusedAudit.reason: Martin authorized the stable patch release on 2026-11-26. The release checklist reserves audits for maintainer requests.

items.text: On phones 375 to 414 points wide at the default interface zoom, the less-used top-bar buttons now move into the "…" menu, so the Settings button is on screen again instead of past the right edge of the bar (discussion #968, #926). At some higher zoom levels part of the button can still be cut off. Checked in browser engines (Chromium, WebKitGTK); not verified on a real iPhone.

regressionEvidence.reason: The toolbar tier tests and responsive browser probe cover narrow layouts. The catalog records Chromium and WebKitGTK evidence at default zoom. A physical iPhone remains unverified.

docs.reason: The Guide already directs users to the gear at the top right.

website.reason: The public Guide already identifies the Settings button by its icon and location.

blog.reason: Covered in the patch release notes.

items.text: A file dropped from the file manager goes after the block under the pointer, and a drop beside the blocks now writes nothing and says "Drop a file onto a block to insert it.", as in Logseq. Before, such a drop could link the file into an older journal file that was not on screen. On Linux and macOS with a display scale above 100%, the drop point is no longer shifted up and to the left of the pointer (#1039, UI-GH1039-FILE-DROP-TARGET).

regressionEvidence.reason: The render regression covers a drop on a routed page, refusal beside the blocks, and platform coordinate conversion. Native macOS, Windows, and fractional-scale Wayland remain unverified.

docs.reason: The Guide already directs users to drop a file onto a block.

website.reason: The public document workflow already shows where to drop a PDF.

blog.reason: Covered in the patch release notes.

items.text: Settings → Graph → Git no longer wipes what you type: the sign-in username and the commit interval keep your text while the git status refreshes, and a refused sign-in keeps the username (only the token is cleared). If the git status refresh reports the repository's remote on another server while the sign-in form is open, the form starts fresh for that server instead of keeping the previous server's name and token (#1035, UI-GH1035-GIT-FIELDS-KEEP-TYPING).

regressionEvidence.reason: The render tests exercise refresh while typing, refused sign-in, and a reported server change. The native journey exercises interval entry with real keys.

docs.reason: The existing Git sign-in and automatic commit instructions still apply.

website.reason: The public Guide already describes the Git setup workflow.

blog.reason: Covered in the patch release notes.

items.text: On macOS, Cmd+Y redoes, as it does in Logseq, next to Cmd+Shift+Z; before, it did nothing. Ctrl+Y stays the system's yank there, and stays Redo's second key on Windows and Linux. Settings → Shortcuts stops showing this second key once the graph's `config.edn` or this device binds Redo (#1044, UI-GH1044-MAC-CMD-Y-REDO).

regressionEvidence.reason: The render tests cover the editor shortcut and the Settings shortcut list on simulated macOS and Linux. Native macOS remains unverified.

docs.reason: The bundled Guide lists the macOS Redo shortcut and explains remapping.

website.reason: The public shortcuts page and interactive Guide include the updated Redo tip.

blog.reason: Covered in the patch release notes.
